Thanks Grace — adding technical color. High-level recommendation for Olive's profile:

1) Model and quantization
- Start with a validated 7B-class model we have in catalog that supports int8. Int8 usually reduces inference cost ~2-3x vs fp16 with minimal quality delta for retrieval/chat-style prompts after a short calibration pass.
- Run a lightweight A/B eval on 2k representative prompts to validate hallucination/answer-rate tolerance before moving pilot traffic to quantized variant.

2) Caching and KV strategy
- Prefix/KV cache: you can expect 15-35% token cost reduction if the cache hit rate is high for repeated prefixes (e.g., search templates, static system prompts). Cache TTL should match session patterns — for conversational search we recommend 30–120s sliding window.

3) Batching and latency
- For p95 < 300ms target with peaks to 250qps: continuous batching with micro-batches (4–12 tokens grouping, sub-10ms queueing) keeps latency tight while increasing GPU utilization.
- If you need guaranteed p95 SLAs, Dedicated (reserved pools) is the right path — hosted with autoscale is fine for pilot but has transient cold-starts.

4) Ops and guardrails
- Instrumented eval hooks (we can provide an eval suite) + automatic fallback to fp16 model variant for rare failure modes.

Implication for pricing / commits: if you plan to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (dedicated or committed-hosted band) we can price quantized usage at a lower unit rate as a standard concession, and include up to 40 hours of implementation support in the pilot credits. For a hosted pilot we typically hold the 20–25% effective discount band.

Happy to join a technical sync next week to scope the evaluation set and sample traffic.

-Marcus
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
